title: Thrown and altered oval bowl
subtitle: A stoneware bowl thrown as a circle then squeezed into an oval shape at leather-hard
excerpt: Throwing and altering combines the speed of the wheel with a hand-altered shape. The bowl is thrown as a circle, allowed to stiffen to leather-hard, then gently squeezed into an oval by hand. The oval changes the bowl's visual weight and makes it better suited to bread, fruit, or serving dishes than a round bowl.
sourceNotes: Thrown and altered oval bowl derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: The stage at which the bowl is stiff enough to hold its shape when squeezed into an oval without collapsing
A technique where a wheel-thrown form is modified by hand at leather-hard to create a non-circular shape
First firing to cone 06 (approx 1000 degrees C)
Pyrometric measure of heat-work in a kiln. Cone 6 approx 1220 degrees C

content.text: Silica dust is the chronic studio hazard. Silicosis is irreversible. Mix wet whenever possible. Wear a P100 respirator any time raw glaze powders are open. Wet-clean only: no sweeping, no dry sanding indoors. Adequate ventilation when firing. Do not open a hot kiln below 80 degrees C.
Throwing and altering

gives forms that could not be produced on the wheel alone. The bowl is thrown as a wide, shallow circle , about 250 mm diameter and 70 mm tall , then at leather-hard, both hands are placed on opposite sides of the rim and pressed inward to compress the circle into an oval. Grogged stoneware handles the altering stress better than smooth clay.

materials.name: Mid-fire glaze, pre-mixed (in a bucket for dipping)

content.text: Throw the circular bowl
Wedge 1 kg of grogged stoneware. Centre on the wheel head.

Open a wide floor , 100 mm across, leaving 10 mm at the base. Pull the walls upward and outward in three passes to create a wide, open bowl form. Target 250 mm rim diameter and 70 mm height. The bowl should be clearly wide and flat , a serving bowl profile, not a high cylinder.
Compress the inside floor with the rib to prevent cracking as the base dries. Smooth and compress the rim with the chamois.
Wire off and allow to dry to leather-hard on a board. This takes 3-5 hours at room temperature for a bowl this size.
Alter to oval at leather-hard
At
leather-hard
, the clay should feel firm and cool, holding its shape but with a very slight flex , place both palms flat on opposite sides of the rim.

Apply gentle, even pressure inward on both sides simultaneously. The circle will begin to compress into an oval. Do this in three or four gradual presses rather than one hard squeeze , the wall may crack if you push too fast.

Stop when the bowl is oval with a long axis about 300 mm and a short axis about 200 mm. Check the rim is still level , the altering step can cause one side to drop. Re-level with light hand pressure if needed.
Allow the altered bowl to finish drying on a flat surface without further disturbance.
Trim, bisque, and glaze

Trim the base at leather-hard. The oval cannot be centred on the wheel for trimming; place it on the banding wheel and trim freehand with the loop tool. Create a foot-ring to match the oval base perimeter.
Allow to bone-dry.
Bisque
fire at
cone
06. Dip-glaze the whole bowl, inside and outside, using the glaze bucket and tongs. Clean the foot-ring of glaze. Glaze-fire to cone 6 (1220 degrees C).

rows.problem: Bowl cracked along the sides during altering
rows.cause: Clay was too dry when squeezed , at bone-dry stage, the clay cannot flex
rows.fix: Check leather-hard readiness: the clay should feel cool and firm but not hard. Lightly mist the outside if the clay has dried too much before altering.

rows.cause: One side was pressed more than the other, or the rim was uneven before altering
rows.fix: Re-level the rim at leather-hard with gentle hand pressure while the bowl is on a flat surface.
